import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import RectBivariateSpline

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.arange(350, dtype=float)
y = np.arange(850, dtype=float)
z = np.random.randint(0, 100, size=(350, 850), dtype=float)

# Create the spline with non-zero smoothing
spl = RectBivariateSpline(x, y, z, s=1)

# Evaluate at the training points
z_eval = spl(x, y, grid=False)

# Check for NaN values
nan_count = np.isnan(z_eval).sum()
has_nan = bool(np.isnan(z_eval).any())
max_val = np.nanmax(z_eval) if not has_nan else np.inf
min_val = np.nanmin(z_eval) if not has_nan else np.inf

probe('nan_count_s1', nan_count)
probe('has_nan_s1', float(has_nan))
probe('max_value_s1', max_val)
probe('min_value_s1', min_val)

import numpy as np

import traceback

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

def check_spline_quality(x, y, z, spl, z_spl, atol, rtol, test_name):
    """Helper to check and record spline quality metrics."""
    has_nan = np.isnan(z_spl).any()
    probe(f"{test_name}::has_nan", has_nan)
    
    if not has_nan:
        # Check how close the spline evaluation is to original data
        diff = np.abs(z_spl - z)
        max_abs_error = np.max(diff)
        probe(f"{test_name}::max_abs_error", max_abs_error)
        
        # Check relative error
        with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
            rel_error = diff / (np.abs(z) + 1e-10)
            max_rel_error = np.nanmax(rel_error)
        probe(f"{test_name}::max_rel_error", max_rel_error)
        
        # Check if within tolerance
        within_atol = np.all(diff <= atol)
        within_rtol = np.all(rel_error <= rtol)
        probe(f"{test_name}::within_atol", within_atol)
        probe(f"{test_name}::within_rtol", within_rtol)
